title: Hal Higdon Advanced 10K Training Program (8 weeks)
population: Advanced runners who compete regularly in races up to 10K or beyond and can run 30-60 min a day, 5-7 days a week
findings: Sunday long run by week: 6, 7, 8 (3/1), 5K race, 8 (3/1), 8K race, 10 (3/1) miles, then the 10K race in week 8.
Weeks 4 and 6 replace the long run with a 5K and an 8K race.
Typical week has 7 runs: Tuesday 30-60 min tempo, Wednesday 400 m repeats, easy runs of 3-6 miles, and a Saturday pace run of 5-6 miles.
Peak long run is 10 miles (16.1 km) with the final quarter near race pace; the page gives no minutes, and 10 miles at an easy pace is roughly 80-100 min (estimate, not stated on the page).
limitations: Read through a page-fetch summariser that restated the table, so weekly cells are not verbatim. Convention, not evidence; no outcome data. Year is the access date, not a publication date.
implications: Peak long run of 10 miles (about 16 km, 80-100 min) is a sensible high-volume ceiling for a 10 km goal and equals Jay Johnson's maximum for a serious 10K runner.
Most long runs in this plan are 6-8 miles; only the last is 10, so a 10 km plan's peak long run can sit near 75-90 min.
